questions.prompt: Which statement best shows self-awareness in a Grade 8 learner?
options: I understand my strengths and areas I need to improve.
I always wait for others to decide for me.
I hide all my mistakes from everyone.
I blame classmates whenever work is difficult.
questions.correctAnswer: I understand my strengths and areas I need to improve.
questions.explanation: Self-awareness means knowing your feelings, strengths, values, habits, and areas for growth.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize personal strengths and areas for improvement in learning and daily life.

questions.prompt: A learner notices they become impatient during group work. What is the most useful first response?
options: Accept the feeling and plan how to listen better.
Quit every group task immediately.
Shout so that others stop talking.
Pretend the habit does not exist.
questions.correctAnswer: Accept the feeling and plan how to listen better.
questions.explanation: Recognizing a habit gives the learner a chance to manage it and improve relationships.
questions.learningOutcome: Use self-reflection to identify habits that affect learning and relationships.

questions.prompt: Which example shows a personal value guiding behavior?
options: Returning a lost pen because honesty matters to you
Copying homework because others are doing it
Keeping quiet when a friend is bullied
Skipping duties because they are tiring
questions.correctAnswer: Returning a lost pen because honesty matters to you
questions.explanation: Values are beliefs that guide choices, such as honesty, respect, responsibility, and fairness.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how personal values influence choices and conduct.

questions.prompt: Why is positive self-talk helpful before a class presentation?
options: It can build confidence and reduce fear.
It guarantees that nobody will ask questions.
It removes the need to prepare.
It makes feedback unnecessary.
questions.correctAnswer: It can build confidence and reduce fear.
questions.explanation: Positive self-talk helps a learner focus on effort, preparation, and ability instead of fear.
questions.learningOutcome: Use positive self-talk to build self-esteem and confidence.

questions.prompt: A learner says, "I failed the first try, so I will practise and try a better method." Which attitude is shown?
options: Growth mindset
Helplessness
Peer pressure
Dishonesty
questions.correctAnswer: Growth mindset
questions.explanation: A growth mindset treats mistakes as chances to learn and improve through effort and strategy.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate a growth mindset when facing learning challenges.

questions.prompt: Which goal is written in a clear and measurable way?
options: I will revise Mathematics for 30 minutes each weekday for four weeks.
I will become better at everything soon.
I will study when I feel like it.
I will avoid all difficult subjects.
questions.correctAnswer: I will revise Mathematics for 30 minutes each weekday for four weeks.
questions.explanation: A measurable goal states the action, time, and period so progress can be checked.
questions.learningOutcome: Set clear and measurable personal learning goals.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to improve in Kiswahili but also has sports practice. Which plan best shows self-management?
options: Create a realistic timetable that includes study, practice, rest, and review.
Stop sleeping so there is more time.
Attend only sports and hope marks improve.
Copy notes quickly without understanding them.
questions.correctAnswer: Create a realistic timetable that includes study, practice, rest, and review.
questions.explanation: Self-management balances important responsibilities and includes time for rest and reflection.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop practical plans for balancing school duties and personal goals.

questions.prompt: Which action best helps a learner review progress toward a personal goal?
options: Compare weekly actions with the goal and adjust the plan.
Wait until the term ends before checking.
Ask a friend to guess the progress.
Change the goal every day without reason.
questions.correctAnswer: Compare weekly actions with the goal and adjust the plan.
questions.explanation: Regular review helps a learner notice progress, solve obstacles, and improve the plan.
questions.learningOutcome: Monitor and adjust personal goals using evidence of progress.

questions.prompt: Which situation shows responsible independence?
options: Completing assigned work and asking for help when genuinely stuck
Refusing all guidance from adults
Doing only tasks that are easy
Ignoring school rules to prove confidence
questions.correctAnswer: Completing assigned work and asking for help when genuinely stuck
questions.explanation: Responsible independence combines initiative with willingness to seek support when needed.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate responsible independence in school and home tasks.

questions.prompt: A learner receives feedback that their project lacks evidence. What response best supports personal growth?
options: Ask which evidence is missing and revise the project.
Tear up the project in anger.
Ignore the teacher and submit the same work.
Tell others that feedback is always unfair.
questions.correctAnswer: Ask which evidence is missing and revise the project.
questions.explanation: Constructive use of feedback helps learners improve work and build confidence.
questions.learningOutcome: Use feedback to improve personal performance and learning habits.

questions.prompt: Which question would best help a learner explore career interests responsibly?
options: Which subjects, talents, values, and community needs connect with this career?
Which career lets me avoid learning new skills?
Which job sounds popular this week only?
Which career can I choose without asking questions?
questions.correctAnswer: Which subjects, talents, values, and community needs connect with this career?
questions.explanation: Career exploration should consider abilities, interests, values, required learning, and service to society.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how personal talents and values can inform future career choices.

questions.prompt: A learner is designing a personal improvement plan after low test scores. Which plan is strongest?
options: Identify weak topics, schedule practice, seek support, and review scores weekly.
Hide the result and stop attending lessons.
Read only the easiest notes once.
Wait for classmates to solve the problem.
questions.correctAnswer: Identify weak topics, schedule practice, seek support, and review scores weekly.
questions.explanation: A strong plan names the problem, sets actions, uses support, and checks progress.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a realistic plan for improving personal learning outcomes.

questions.prompt: What is an emotion?
options: A feeling such as joy, fear, anger, or sadness
A school rule written in a book
A type of exam timetable
A permanent mark on a report card
questions.correctAnswer: A feeling such as joy, fear, anger, or sadness
questions.explanation: Emotions are feelings that can influence thoughts, behavior, and decisions.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common emotions and how they affect behaviour.

questions.prompt: Which body sign may show that a learner is stressed?
options: Headache, tiredness, or difficulty concentrating
Perfect memory at all times
No reaction to pressure
Always finishing every task early
questions.correctAnswer: Headache, tiredness, or difficulty concentrating
questions.explanation: Stress can affect the body and mind, including sleep, concentration, mood, and energy.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize physical and emotional signs of stress.

questions.prompt: A learner feels angry after being teased. Which response shows self-control?
options: Pause, breathe, and report the teasing calmly.
Hit the person immediately.
Spread false stories online.
Break nearby property.
questions.correctAnswer: Pause, breathe, and report the teasing calmly.
questions.explanation: Self-control helps a learner respond safely and seek support instead of escalating harm.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply self-control strategies when experiencing strong emotions.

questions.prompt: Which method is a healthy way to cope with examination pressure?
options: Prepare early, take breaks, sleep well, and ask for help.
Stay awake every night until the exam.
Drink unknown pills to stay alert.
Avoid all revision because pressure exists.
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare early, take breaks, sleep well, and ask for help.
questions.explanation: Healthy coping reduces stress while protecting learning, safety, and wellbeing.
questions.learningOutcome: Use healthy coping strategies to manage academic pressure.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows resilience after a disappointment?
options: Learn from the experience and try again with support.
Give up all related activities forever.
Blame everyone and refuse help.
Pretend the disappointment never happened.
questions.correctAnswer: Learn from the experience and try again with support.
questions.explanation: Resilience is the ability to recover from setbacks and keep working toward positive goals.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate resilience when dealing with setbacks and disappointments.

questions.prompt: A learner feels overwhelmed by family duties and school tasks. Which support-seeking action is most appropriate?
options: Talk to a trusted adult and agree on a manageable plan.
Run away from home without telling anyone.
Stop attending school quietly.
Insult family members until duties disappear.
questions.correctAnswer: Talk to a trusted adult and agree on a manageable plan.
questions.explanation: Seeking help from trusted adults can reduce pressure and lead to safer, practical solutions.
questions.learningOutcome: Seek appropriate support when personal pressure becomes difficult to manage.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to name an emotion before responding to it?
options: It helps a person choose a safer and more thoughtful response.
It makes the emotion disappear immediately.
It proves that the other person is wrong.
It removes the need to solve the problem.
questions.correctAnswer: It helps a person choose a safer and more thoughtful response.
questions.explanation: Naming an emotion creates a pause for thinking and helps prevent harmful reactions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how emotional awareness supports responsible behavior.

questions.prompt: A learner is anxious before performing a poem. Which strategy is most useful just before going on stage?
options: Take slow breaths and focus on the first lines.
Read unrelated messages until called.
Tell themselves they will certainly fail.
Argue with classmates to release tension.
questions.correctAnswer: Take slow breaths and focus on the first lines.
questions.explanation: Breathing and focusing attention can calm the body and support confident performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply simple anxiety management strategies in school activities.

questions.prompt: Which choice best balances digital entertainment and wellbeing?
options: Set screen limits, finish duties, rest, and do physical activity.
Play games all night before school.
Skip meals to watch videos.
Stop talking to family because of online chats.
questions.correctAnswer: Set screen limits, finish duties, rest, and do physical activity.
questions.explanation: Balanced living includes learning, rest, social connection, physical activity, and responsible media use.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan routines that balance learning, recreation, rest, and wellbeing.

questions.prompt: Which situation requires urgent help from a trusted adult or health worker?
options: A learner talks about harming themselves.
A learner dislikes one homework task.
A learner asks for extra revision notes.
A learner changes a club meeting time.
questions.correctAnswer: A learner talks about harming themselves.
questions.explanation: Talk of self-harm is serious and should be reported immediately so the learner gets protection and support.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify situations that require immediate support from trusted adults or professionals.

questions.prompt: A classmate becomes quiet, withdraws from friends, and stops submitting work. What is the most caring response?
options: Check on them respectfully and inform a trusted teacher if concern continues.
Mock them for being quiet.
Post about them online.
Ignore them because it is not your problem.
questions.correctAnswer: Check on them respectfully and inform a trusted teacher if concern continues.
questions.explanation: Empathy and responsible help-seeking can connect a struggling person with support.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse signs that a peer may need support and respond respectfully.

questions.prompt: Which plan best helps a learner manage anger during repeated provocation?
options: Identify triggers, practise calming steps, avoid retaliation, and seek mediation.
Plan revenge after school.
Save angry messages to send later.
Ignore all school rules until others apologise.
questions.correctAnswer: Identify triggers, practise calming steps, avoid retaliation, and seek mediation.
questions.explanation: A strong anger-management plan combines self-awareness, self-control, safety, and support.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a practical plan for managing anger and avoiding harmful responses.

questions.prompt: Why should learners avoid using alcohol or drugs to handle stress?
options: They can harm health, judgment, learning, and relationships.
They always solve stress permanently.
They make school rules unnecessary.
They remove all consequences of choices.
questions.correctAnswer: They can harm health, judgment, learning, and relationships.
questions.explanation: Substance use is an unsafe coping method and can create serious health and social problems.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why substance use is an unsafe way to cope with stress.

questions.prompt: What is active listening?
options: Paying full attention and showing you understand the speaker
Planning your reply while ignoring the speaker
Interrupting until the speaker stops
Changing the topic whenever possible
questions.correctAnswer: Paying full attention and showing you understand the speaker
questions.explanation: Active listening uses attention, respectful body language, and checking understanding.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify behaviours that show active listening.

questions.prompt: Which phrase is an assertive way to refuse unsafe peer pressure?
options: No, I will not do that because it is unsafe.
Maybe I will do it if everyone laughs.
I must obey you even when I disagree.
Let us hide it from the teacher first.
questions.correctAnswer: No, I will not do that because it is unsafe.
questions.explanation: Assertiveness means expressing a clear position respectfully without aggression.
questions.learningOutcome: Use assertive language to resist unsafe pressure.

questions.prompt: Which statement uses an I-message during a disagreement?
options: I feel ignored when I am interrupted, so please let me finish.
You are always bad at listening.
Everyone knows you are the problem.
Stop talking or I will report you.
questions.correctAnswer: I feel ignored when I am interrupted, so please let me finish.
questions.explanation: An I-message explains feelings and needs without attacking the other person.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply respectful communication during disagreements.

questions.prompt: A group member has not done their part of a project. Which response is most constructive?
options: Ask what happened, agree on a new deadline, and offer reasonable support.
Remove their name without any discussion.
Shout at them in front of the class.
Do nothing and blame them during presentation.
questions.correctAnswer: Ask what happened, agree on a new deadline, and offer reasonable support.
questions.explanation: Constructive communication addresses the problem while preserving respect and responsibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Use respectful communication to improve teamwork and shared responsibility.

questions.prompt: Which behaviour shows empathy toward a new learner in class?
options: Inviting them to join a group and explaining routines kindly
Laughing at their accent
Keeping all class information from them
Leaving them alone during every activity
questions.correctAnswer: Inviting them to join a group and explaining routines kindly
questions.explanation: Empathy means trying to understand another person's experience and responding with care.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate empathy and inclusion in school relationships.

questions.prompt: Which friendship quality is most likely to support a learner's wellbeing?
options: Mutual respect, honesty, and encouragement
Pressure to break rules
Mocking personal goals
Keeping secrets about danger
questions.correctAnswer: Mutual respect, honesty, and encouragement
questions.explanation: Healthy friendships support good choices, respect boundaries, and encourage personal growth.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe qualities of healthy and supportive friendships.

questions.prompt: A friend asks to copy your homework and says true friends help each other. What is the best response?
options: Refuse copying and offer to explain the work instead.
Give them the book because friendship has no limits.
Copy their work next time as payment.
Avoid all future schoolwork together.
questions.correctAnswer: Refuse copying and offer to explain the work instead.
questions.explanation: Healthy help supports learning without dishonesty or unfair advantage.
questions.learningOutcome: Set respectful boundaries in friendships while offering appropriate support.

questions.prompt: Which action best prevents bullying in a school setting?
options: Report bullying, support the target, and refuse to join in.
Record and share the bullying for fun.
Encourage others to laugh.
Tell the target to keep quiet forever.
questions.correctAnswer: Report bullying, support the target, and refuse to join in.
questions.explanation: Bullying prevention requires reporting harm, supporting affected learners, and refusing harmful group behaviour.
questions.learningOutcome: Take responsible action to prevent and report bullying.

questions.prompt: A disagreement between two learners is growing tense. Which step should come before deciding on a solution?
options: Allow each person to explain their view respectfully.
Force one person to apologise without listening.
Spread the disagreement to other classes.
Hide the issue until it becomes worse.
questions.correctAnswer: Allow each person to explain their view respectfully.
questions.explanation: Conflict resolution begins with listening to understand the issue and each person's needs.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply peaceful steps for resolving interpersonal conflicts.

questions.prompt: What is mediation?
options: A neutral person helping others discuss a conflict and find a fair solution
A person choosing a winner without listening
A group spreading rumours about a conflict
A way to punish both people without evidence
questions.correctAnswer: A neutral person helping others discuss a conflict and find a fair solution
questions.explanation: Mediation supports peaceful discussion and agreement without taking sides.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of mediation in peaceful conflict resolution.

questions.prompt: Which action shows respect for diversity in a school club?
options: Listening to different opinions and sharing roles fairly
Excluding learners from other communities
Mocking religious or cultural practices
Letting one group make every decision
questions.correctAnswer: Listening to different opinions and sharing roles fairly
questions.explanation: Respect for diversity values different backgrounds, abilities, ideas, and beliefs.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate respect for diversity in school and community interactions.

questions.prompt: A peer group tells a learner to skip a lesson to prove loyalty. Which analysis is best?
options: The group is using negative peer pressure that can harm learning.
The group is showing responsible teamwork.
The learner must obey because friends decide values.
Skipping lessons has no consequences.
questions.correctAnswer: The group is using negative peer pressure that can harm learning.
questions.explanation: Negative peer pressure pushes someone toward harmful, unsafe, or irresponsible choices.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse positive and negative peer influence in everyday situations.

questions.prompt: Which response best repairs trust after a learner breaks a group agreement?
options: Admit the mistake, apologise, make amends, and keep future promises.
Deny everything even when evidence exists.
Blame the quietest group member.
Promise change but repeat the same behaviour immediately.
questions.correctAnswer: Admit the mistake, apologise, make amends, and keep future promises.
questions.explanation: Trust is rebuilt through honesty, responsibility, changed behaviour, and consistency.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse actions that rebuild trust after conflict or wrongdoing.

questions.prompt: A class committee must choose roles for a clean-up project. Which plan is fairest?
options: Match roles to abilities, rotate duties, and allow members to contribute ideas.
Give all visible roles to close friends.
Assign difficult tasks to one learner only.
Let no one question the leader.
questions.correctAnswer: Match roles to abilities, rotate duties, and allow members to contribute ideas.
questions.explanation: Fair teamwork uses participation, strengths, shared responsibility, and accountability.
questions.learningOutcome: Create fair teamwork arrangements that include different abilities and voices.

questions.prompt: Which feedback is most helpful after a group presentation?
options: Your examples were clear; next time speak louder for the back row.
That was bad and you know it.
Nobody understood anything.
You should never present again.
questions.correctAnswer: Your examples were clear; next time speak louder for the back row.
questions.explanation: Helpful feedback is specific, respectful, and points to a practical improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Give specific and respectful feedback that supports improvement.

questions.prompt: What is responsible decision making?
options: Choosing after considering values, facts, options, and consequences
Choosing the quickest option without thinking
Following the loudest person every time
Avoiding every decision until others suffer
questions.correctAnswer: Choosing after considering values, facts, options, and consequences
questions.explanation: Responsible decisions consider information, values, possible outcomes, and people affected.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the meaning of responsible decision making.

questions.prompt: Which step should come before choosing among several options?
options: Think about likely consequences of each option.
Announce the choice before checking facts.
Copy the choice of the most popular learner.
Ignore anyone affected by the decision.
questions.correctAnswer: Think about likely consequences of each option.
questions.explanation: Considering consequences helps a learner choose options that are safer and more responsible.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the role of consequences in responsible decision making.

questions.prompt: A learner finds a phone near the field. Which decision best shows integrity?
options: Take it to a teacher or office so the owner can be found.
Keep it because no one saw it.
Sell it quickly.
Remove the SIM card and hide it.
questions.correctAnswer: Take it to a teacher or office so the owner can be found.
questions.explanation: Integrity means doing the right thing even when no one is watching.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply integrity when making choices about other people's property.

questions.prompt: Which question best helps assess risk before joining an activity?
options: Could this harm my safety, learning, values, or relationships?
Will this make me look fearless for a moment?
Can we hide it from every adult?
Will my friends laugh if I ask questions?
questions.correctAnswer: Could this harm my safety, learning, values, or relationships?
questions.explanation: Risk assessment checks possible harm and helps a learner choose safer alternatives.
questions.learningOutcome: Use risk assessment questions before making choices in peer situations.

questions.prompt: A learner is invited to leave school without permission. Which option is safest?
options: Refuse, stay in school, and report the pressure to a trusted adult.
Leave quickly before being noticed.
Send a false message to the parent.
Agree because friends are waiting.
questions.correctAnswer: Refuse, stay in school, and report the pressure to a trusted adult.
questions.explanation: The safe choice protects the learner, follows school rules, and seeks adult support.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose safe alternatives when facing risky peer pressure.

questions.prompt: Why should a learner gather accurate information before making a serious decision?
options: Accurate information reduces guessing and helps compare choices fairly.
It makes every decision easy and consequence-free.
It allows rumours to spread faster.
It removes personal responsibility.
questions.correctAnswer: Accurate information reduces guessing and helps compare choices fairly.
questions.explanation: Good decisions depend on reliable facts, not rumours or pressure.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why reliable information is important in decision making.

questions.prompt: A team disagrees about how to use limited club funds. Which decision-making method is most responsible?
options: List needs, compare benefits and costs, discuss fairly, and record the choice.
Let the loudest member spend the money.
Use the money secretly before the meeting.
Choose the first idea to avoid discussion.
questions.correctAnswer: List needs, compare benefits and costs, discuss fairly, and record the choice.
questions.explanation: Responsible group decisions use evidence, fairness, transparency, and accountability.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse fair procedures for making decisions in groups.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains problem solving?
options: Identifying a challenge, exploring causes, choosing actions, and checking results
Complaining about a challenge without action
Choosing a random answer quickly
Waiting for the problem to disappear always
questions.correctAnswer: Identifying a challenge, exploring causes, choosing actions, and checking results
questions.explanation: Problem solving is a step-by-step process for moving from a challenge to an improved situation.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe practical steps in solving everyday problems.

questions.prompt: A class notices that litter keeps returning near the school gate. Which action should come first in problem solving?
options: Find out when, why, and by whom litter is being dropped.
Punish a random class immediately.
Paint the gate a brighter colour only.
Ignore the litter until inspection day.
questions.correctAnswer: Find out when, why, and by whom litter is being dropped.
questions.explanation: Understanding causes helps learners choose solutions that fit the real problem.
questions.learningOutcome: Investigate causes of everyday problems before selecting solutions.

questions.prompt: Which choice best shows ethical decision making during an examination?
options: Do your own work and report cheating if required.
Hide notes in a sleeve.
Share answers quietly.
Copy from a nearby script.
questions.correctAnswer: Do your own work and report cheating if required.
questions.explanation: Ethical decisions protect honesty, fairness, and trust in learning.
questions.learningOutcome: Make ethical decisions in school assessment situations.

questions.prompt: A learner must choose between attending revision and watching a football match. The exam is the next day. Which reasoning is strongest?
options: Attend revision first because the exam is urgent and affects learning goals.
Watch the match because entertainment should always come first.
Skip both activities to avoid choosing.
Let a friend decide without explaining why.
questions.correctAnswer: Attend revision first because the exam is urgent and affects learning goals.
questions.explanation: Responsible choices consider priorities, timing, goals, and consequences.
questions.learningOutcome: Use priorities and consequences to make responsible time choices.

questions.prompt: Which decision best protects public property in school?
options: Use desks carefully and report damage early.
Scratch names on desks for fun.
Remove library books without records.
Break a tap to stop others using water.
questions.correctAnswer: Use desks carefully and report damage early.
questions.explanation: Public and shared property should be protected so everyone can benefit from it.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate responsibility when using shared and public resources.

questions.prompt: A friend asks you to keep a secret about a dangerous plan. Which decision is most responsible?
options: Tell a trusted adult because safety is at risk.
Keep the secret no matter what happens.
Join the plan to monitor it secretly.
Post the secret online for everyone.
questions.correctAnswer: Tell a trusted adult because safety is at risk.
questions.explanation: Secrets about danger should be shared with trusted adults to protect people from harm.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse when confidentiality should give way to safety and help seeking.

questions.prompt: A school club wants to solve low attendance at meetings. Which plan is most likely to work?
options: Survey members, identify barriers, adjust meeting time, and track attendance.
Blame absent members without asking why.
Cancel every meeting permanently.
Choose a new name without changing anything else.
questions.correctAnswer: Survey members, identify barriers, adjust meeting time, and track attendance.
questions.explanation: Effective problem solving uses evidence, action, and follow-up to check improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Create an evidence-based action plan for solving a school problem.

questions.prompt: Which factor should be considered most when choosing whether to share a rumour?
options: Whether it is true, kind, necessary, and safe to share
Whether it will attract attention
Whether it embarrasses someone disliked
Whether it can spread before assembly
questions.correctAnswer: Whether it is true, kind, necessary, and safe to share
questions.explanation: Responsible communication considers truth, respect, purpose, and possible harm.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse consequences before sharing information about others.

questions.prompt: Which number is commonly used in Kenya to call police emergency services?
questions.explanation: In Kenya, 999 is a commonly used emergency number for police assistance.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify emergency contacts and safe reporting channels.

questions.prompt: Which action is safest when crossing a busy road?
options: Use a designated crossing and check traffic both ways.
Run across while looking at a phone.
Cross from behind a parked bus without looking.
Follow friends without checking vehicles.
questions.correctAnswer: Use a designated crossing and check traffic both ways.
questions.explanation: Road safety requires visibility, attention, patience, and use of safer crossing points.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify safe pedestrian practices on roads.

questions.prompt: A learner gets a small cut while cleaning the classroom. What should be done first?
options: Wash hands, clean the cut safely, and inform the teacher.
Rub soil on the wound.
Ignore it until it becomes painful.
Share the same dirty cloth with others.
questions.correctAnswer: Wash hands, clean the cut safely, and inform the teacher.
questions.explanation: Basic first aid protects the wound from infection and ensures adult support.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply simple first aid steps for minor cuts and injuries.

questions.prompt: Why should learners avoid taking medicine that was prescribed for someone else?
options: It may be unsafe or unsuitable for their condition.
It always works better if borrowed.
It has no possible side effects.
It removes the need for adult guidance.
questions.correctAnswer: It may be unsafe or unsuitable for their condition.
questions.explanation: Medicine should be used with proper guidance because wrong use can cause harm.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safe practices for using medicine and seeking treatment.

questions.prompt: Which item should be included in a simple home emergency kit?
options: Clean bandage, torch, emergency contacts, and safe drinking water
Open petrol, loose matches, and expired food
Only old magazines
A broken phone with no battery
questions.correctAnswer: Clean bandage, torch, emergency contacts, and safe drinking water
questions.explanation: Emergency kits should include safe, useful items for first aid, communication, light, and basic needs.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare basic items needed for household emergency readiness.

questions.prompt: A fire alarm sounds during a lesson. Which response is safest?
options: Leave calmly through the marked route and assemble at the agreed point.
Run back for a school bag.
Hide under a desk until the bell stops.
Push others to reach the gate first.
questions.correctAnswer: Leave calmly through the marked route and assemble at the agreed point.
questions.explanation: Fire safety requires calm evacuation, use of marked exits, and assembly for head count.
questions.learningOutcome: Follow safe procedures during fire and evacuation drills.

questions.prompt: Which practice helps prevent the spread of communicable diseases in school?
options: Wash hands with soap, cover coughs, and avoid sharing personal items.
Share water bottles with everyone.
Ignore toilets that lack water.
Attend school when advised to isolate for infection.
questions.correctAnswer: Wash hands with soap, cover coughs, and avoid sharing personal items.
questions.explanation: Good hygiene reduces the spread of germs and protects the school community.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe hygiene practices that protect personal and community health.

questions.prompt: Which situation is a personal safety warning sign?
options: An adult asks a learner to keep an uncomfortable secret.
A teacher announces homework openly.
A parent signs a school trip form.
A class captain records attendance.
questions.correctAnswer: An adult asks a learner to keep an uncomfortable secret.
questions.explanation: Uncomfortable secrets, unsafe touch, threats, or isolation should be reported to a trusted adult.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify unsafe situations and seek help from trusted adults.

questions.prompt: During a flood warning, which action is safest for learners walking home?
options: Avoid crossing moving water and follow guidance from responsible adults.
Cross flooded bridges quickly to save time.
Play near drainage channels.
Remove shoes and walk through unknown water.
questions.correctAnswer: Avoid crossing moving water and follow guidance from responsible adults.
questions.explanation: Floodwater can be deep, fast, contaminated, or hide dangerous objects.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe behaviour during floods and other environmental hazards.

questions.prompt: Which action best reduces risk when using public transport?
options: Wait in a safe place, board carefully, use a seat belt if available, and avoid leaning out.
Jump into a moving vehicle.
Distract the driver for entertainment.
Stand at the doorway while the vehicle moves.
questions.correctAnswer: Wait in a safe place, board carefully, use a seat belt if available, and avoid leaning out.
questions.explanation: Safe transport habits reduce injuries and support responsible road use.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe practices when using public or school transport.

questions.prompt: A learner sees exposed electrical wires near a classroom socket. What should they do?
options: Keep away, warn others, and report it to an adult immediately.
Touch the wire to check if it works.
Cover it with wet paper.
Use the socket until it stops working.
questions.correctAnswer: Keep away, warn others, and report it to an adult immediately.
questions.explanation: Exposed wires can cause electric shock or fire and should only be handled by qualified adults.
questions.learningOutcome: Respond safely to electrical hazards in the environment.

questions.prompt: Which comparison best explains why prevention is better than emergency response?
options: Prevention reduces the chance of harm before it occurs.
Prevention means ignoring all possible danger.
Emergency response is never needed by anyone.
Prevention works only after injuries happen.
questions.correctAnswer: Prevention reduces the chance of harm before it occurs.
questions.explanation: Prevention uses planning and safe habits to reduce risks before damage or injury occurs.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the value of preventive safety practices.

questions.prompt: A class wants to improve safety near the school gate. Which plan is strongest?
options: Observe risks, involve teachers and guards, mark safe waiting areas, and review results.
Complain without collecting information.
Block the gate during busy hours.
Wait until an accident happens before acting.
questions.correctAnswer: Observe risks, involve teachers and guards, mark safe waiting areas, and review results.
questions.explanation: A strong safety plan uses evidence, responsible people, clear actions, and follow-up.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a practical action plan for improving safety in the school environment.

questions.prompt: What is a digital footprint?
options: The record of a person's activities and information left online
A mark made by shoes in mud
A password written on paper
A computer's power cable
questions.correctAnswer: The record of a person's activities and information left online
questions.explanation: A digital footprint includes posts, comments, shares, searches, and other online traces.
questions.learningOutcome: Define digital footprint and its effect on personal reputation.

questions.prompt: Which item should usually be kept private online?
options: Home address and account password
A public school motto
A general weather update
A drawing of a tree
questions.correctAnswer: Home address and account password
questions.explanation: Private information can expose a learner to theft, impersonation, or unsafe contact.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify personal information that should be protected online.

questions.prompt: Which password habit is safest?
options: Use a strong private password and change it if it is exposed.
Use your name and birth year for every account.
Share the password with the whole class.
Write the password on a public desk.
questions.correctAnswer: Use a strong private password and change it if it is exposed.
questions.explanation: Strong and private passwords help protect accounts from unauthorised access.
questions.learningOutcome: Use responsible password practices to protect digital accounts.

questions.prompt: A learner receives a message saying they won money and must click a strange link. What should they do?
options: Avoid the link and report the message to a trusted adult.
Click quickly before the offer ends.
Enter a password to test it.
Forward it to all friends.
questions.correctAnswer: Avoid the link and report the message to a trusted adult.
questions.explanation: Strange links may be scams or phishing attempts that steal information or install harmful software.
questions.learningOutcome: Respond safely to suspicious links and digital messages.

questions.prompt: Which online comment shows respectful digital communication?
options: I disagree with your point because the source says something different.
You are foolish and should stop posting.
Everyone should laugh at this learner.
I will share your private photo now.
questions.correctAnswer: I disagree with your point because the source says something different.
questions.explanation: Respectful digital communication can disagree with ideas without insulting or harming people.
questions.learningOutcome: Communicate respectfully and responsibly in digital spaces.

questions.prompt: Before sharing a news item in a class group, which action is most responsible?
options: Check the source, date, evidence, and whether it could harm others.
Share it quickly if the headline is exciting.
Remove the author's name to make it shorter.
Add extra claims to make it more interesting.
questions.correctAnswer: Check the source, date, evidence, and whether it could harm others.
questions.explanation: Responsible media sharing requires checking accuracy, context, and possible harm.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse digital information for reliability before sharing.

questions.prompt: Why should learners ask permission before posting another person's photo?
options: People have a right to privacy and control over their image.
Photos online automatically belong to everyone.
Permission is only needed for adults.
Posting without permission can never harm anyone.
questions.correctAnswer: People have a right to privacy and control over their image.
questions.explanation: Consent protects privacy, dignity, and safety in digital spaces.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply consent and privacy principles when sharing digital content.

questions.prompt: Which action is cyberbullying?
options: Creating a group chat to insult and exclude a learner
Sending homework instructions politely
Sharing a teacher-approved revision link
Asking a respectful question online
questions.correctAnswer: Creating a group chat to insult and exclude a learner
questions.explanation: Cyberbullying uses digital tools to harass, shame, threaten, or exclude others.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify cyberbullying and take safe reporting action.

questions.prompt: A learner has posted an angry comment about a classmate. What is the best way to reduce harm?
options: Delete it, apologise, and avoid posting when angry in future.
Add more insults to explain the first comment.
Ask others to share it before it is removed.
Pretend someone else used the account.
questions.correctAnswer: Delete it, apologise, and avoid posting when angry in future.
questions.explanation: Responsible repair includes removing harmful content, taking responsibility, and changing behaviour.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse ways to repair harm caused by irresponsible digital communication.

questions.prompt: Which digital habit best supports learning during homework time?
options: Use the device for the task, avoid unrelated sites, and save work safely.
Keep many entertainment apps open while studying.
Copy answers without understanding them.
Leave the device unlocked in a public place.
questions.correctAnswer: Use the device for the task, avoid unrelated sites, and save work safely.
questions.explanation: Purposeful technology use supports concentration, learning, and data safety.
questions.learningOutcome: Use digital devices responsibly for learning tasks.

questions.prompt: A group is making a digital poster about road safety. Which plan is most ethical?
options: Use truthful messages, credited images, and respectful language.
Copy another poster and remove the name.
Use frightening false statistics.
Include private photos without permission.
questions.correctAnswer: Use truthful messages, credited images, and respectful language.
questions.explanation: Ethical digital creation respects truth, ownership, privacy, and audience wellbeing.
questions.learningOutcome: Create digital content that is truthful, respectful, and responsible.

questions.prompt: Which choice best protects a learner's reputation online?
options: Think before posting and avoid content that harms self or others.
Post every private feeling immediately.
Join insults so others accept you.
Share passwords to show trust.
questions.correctAnswer: Think before posting and avoid content that harms self or others.
questions.explanation: Online posts can remain visible and affect relationships, safety, and future opportunities.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply responsible posting habits to protect digital reputation.

questions.prompt: What is a need?
options: Something necessary for health, safety, or basic living
Anything wanted for fun only
A luxury bought after saving
A gift that must be expensive
questions.correctAnswer: Something necessary for health, safety, or basic living
questions.explanation: Needs include essentials such as food, water, shelter, health care, and learning materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish needs from wants in everyday choices.

questions.prompt: What is saving?
options: Keeping part of available money or resources for future use
Spending all money immediately
Borrowing without a repayment plan
Hiding records from family members
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping part of available money or resources for future use
questions.explanation: Saving helps people prepare for planned needs, emergencies, and future goals.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning and purpose of saving.

questions.prompt: A learner has KES 200 for the week. Which choice shows budgeting?
options: Plan transport, lunch, savings, and small expenses before spending.
Spend all the money on the first day.
Buy wants first and ignore transport.
Give no thought to future needs.
questions.correctAnswer: Plan transport, lunch, savings, and small expenses before spending.
questions.explanation: A budget helps a person plan how income will meet needs, wants, and savings.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare simple personal budgets for responsible money use.

questions.prompt: Which example shows opportunity cost?
options: Choosing a set book means giving up a snack you could have bought.
Receiving money without spending any of it.
Finding a free library book.
Writing down two prices on paper.
questions.correctAnswer: Choosing a set book means giving up a snack you could have bought.
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the next best option given up when a choice is made.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain opportunity cost in personal spending decisions.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to save KES 600 in six weeks. Which plan is clearest?
options: Save KES 100 each week and record the balance.
Save any amount only if reminded.
Spend first and save what is left by chance.
Borrow KES 600 without a plan.
questions.correctAnswer: Save KES 100 each week and record the balance.
questions.explanation: A clear savings plan states the target, amount per period, and tracking method.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply simple saving plans to meet personal goals.

questions.prompt: Which habit shows care for shared school resources?
options: Use books carefully, return them on time, and report damage.
Hide library books so others cannot use them.
Tear pages needed for homework.
Write jokes on laboratory tables.
questions.correctAnswer: Use books carefully, return them on time, and report damage.
questions.explanation: Shared resources should be protected so current and future learners can benefit.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate responsible care for shared learning resources.

questions.prompt: A club has KES 1,000 and must buy cleaning gloves, sacks, and drinking water for volunteers. What should guide spending?
options: Prioritise safety and essential project needs before extras.
Buy decorations before safety items.
Spend on snacks only.
Let one member keep the money without records.
questions.correctAnswer: Prioritise safety and essential project needs before extras.
questions.explanation: Responsible budgeting gives priority to essential needs and keeps the project safe and accountable.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply budgeting priorities in small group projects.

questions.prompt: Which practice shows financial integrity in a class project?
options: Record income and spending honestly with receipts where possible.
Change figures to hide missing money.
Use group money for personal airtime.
Refuse to let members see records.
questions.correctAnswer: Record income and spending honestly with receipts where possible.
questions.explanation: Financial integrity requires honesty, evidence, transparency, and responsible use of money.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse ethical practices in managing group resources.

questions.prompt: A learner's planned transport cost rises from KES 80 to KES 120. What is the best budget response?
options: Adjust the budget and reduce a lower-priority expense.
Ignore the change and spend as before.
Stop recording expenses.
Borrow secretly without repayment plans.
questions.correctAnswer: Adjust the budget and reduce a lower-priority expense.
questions.explanation: Budgets should be reviewed when costs change so important needs are still met.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how to adjust a budget when income or expenses change.

questions.prompt: A class wants to reduce water waste. Which plan is most practical?
options: Monitor taps, report leaks, assign duty checks, and compare monthly use.
Lock all toilets every day.
Leave taps running to test drainage.
Tell learners to stop drinking water.
questions.correctAnswer: Monitor taps, report leaks, assign duty checks, and compare monthly use.
questions.explanation: A practical resource plan uses observation, responsibility, repair, and evidence of improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple plan for conserving school resources.

questions.prompt: What is community service?
options: Voluntary action that helps improve the community
Work done only for punishment
A way to avoid school responsibilities
Keeping all benefits for one person
questions.correctAnswer: Voluntary action that helps improve the community
questions.explanation: Community service helps meet real needs and builds responsibility, empathy, and citizenship.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning and value of community service.

questions.prompt: Which activity is a suitable community service project for Grade 8 learners with adult guidance?
options: Organising a safe clean-up of the school compound
Entering a restricted construction site alone
Collecting medicine for strangers without permission
Confronting suspected criminals at night
questions.correctAnswer: Organising a safe clean-up of the school compound
questions.explanation: Suitable service projects should be safe, supervised, useful, and age appropriate.
questions.learningOutcome: Select safe and age-appropriate community service activities.

questions.prompt: Which action shows integrity in leadership?
options: Using resources for the agreed purpose and giving clear reports
Favouring friends with every role
Hiding mistakes from members
Changing records to look successful
questions.correctAnswer: Using resources for the agreed purpose and giving clear reports
questions.explanation: Integrity in leadership means honesty, fairness, accountability, and service.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe leadership behaviours that show integrity and accountability.

questions.prompt: A class wants to plant trees in the community. Which question should they ask first?
options: Which site needs trees, who owns it, and who will care for seedlings?
Which site is farthest from water?
How can we finish without permission?
How can we plant trees and never monitor them?
questions.correctAnswer: Which site needs trees, who owns it, and who will care for seedlings?
questions.explanation: Planning a service project requires need assessment, permission, resources, and follow-up care.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan environmental service activities using community needs and sustainability.

questions.prompt: Which behaviour best promotes peace during a school competition?
options: Respect rules, accept results fairly, and congratulate others.
Insult the winning team.
Destroy equipment after losing.
Spread rumours about judges.
questions.correctAnswer: Respect rules, accept results fairly, and congratulate others.
questions.explanation: Peaceful participation shows sportsmanship, respect, self-control, and fairness.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate peaceful and respectful participation in school activities.

questions.prompt: A learner notices a classmate being excluded because of disability. Which response supports inclusion?
options: Ask how they can participate and adapt roles fairly.
Assume they cannot contribute.
Hide activity information from them.
Let others make jokes about them.
questions.correctAnswer: Ask how they can participate and adapt roles fairly.
questions.explanation: Inclusion removes unnecessary barriers and respects every person's dignity and ability to contribute.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply inclusive practices that respect dignity and different abilities.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best shows that a clean-up project was successful?
options: Reduced litter, proper waste disposal, and regular follow-up records
Only the number of selfies taken
A speech made before work began
A rumour that the compound looks better
questions.correctAnswer: Reduced litter, proper waste disposal, and regular follow-up records
questions.explanation: Project success should be judged using observable evidence and records, not only impressions.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate community service projects using observable evidence.

questions.prompt: A youth group wants to address noise complaints near a study area. Which solution respects all users?
options: Hold dialogue, agree on quiet hours, and identify alternative play times.
Ban all games permanently without discussion.
Ignore learners who need quiet.
Shout louder to prove the complaint is wrong.
questions.correctAnswer: Hold dialogue, agree on quiet hours, and identify alternative play times.
questions.explanation: Respectful community problem solving balances needs through dialogue and fair agreements.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse peaceful ways of balancing different community needs.

questions.prompt: Which plan best prepares learners to lead a peer hygiene campaign?
options: Research key messages, assign roles, prepare materials, present, and gather feedback.
Start shouting instructions without facts.
Copy posters without checking accuracy.
Let one learner do everything alone.
questions.correctAnswer: Research key messages, assign roles, prepare materials, present, and gather feedback.
questions.explanation: A strong campaign plan uses accurate information, teamwork, communication, and evaluation.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a peer education plan for promoting healthy community practices.

questions.prompt: A class must choose one service project from three possible ideas. Which decision process is best?
options: Compare community need, safety, resources, learner skills, and expected impact.
Choose the idea suggested by the most popular learner.
Pick the project with no plan because it sounds exciting.
Avoid all service because decisions take time.
questions.correctAnswer: Compare community need, safety, resources, learner skills, and expected impact.
questions.explanation: Good service planning weighs need, feasibility, safety, resources, participation, and impact.
questions.learningOutcome: Create criteria for selecting realistic and useful service learning projects.
